newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends firmer v dollar in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends firmer v dollar in dull trade.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed firmer against the dollar on Tuesday on some import covering but off the day's highs, dealers said.
"Spot traded down to 57.61 and closed slightly higher at 57.68 rupees with late evening demand from import covering," said Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation dealer.
The rupee opened slightly stronger against the greenback at 57.75 after closing on Monday at 57.79. It closed at 57.77 on Friday.
"Very few banks were covering imports. Some speculators were selling dollars," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed the U.S. currency down by half a local cent despite the dollar's slight weakening overseas. It fixed buying and selling rates at 57.0997 and 58.2533 respectively.
"Internationally, the dollar is weaker so we do not expect any depreciation of the rupee unless something in New York triggers the dollar to appreciate," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates closed at around 11 percent after opening at 12 percent. "The money market is very liquid," said a dealer.
